name: Shelumiel
overview: Shelumiel was a male leader from the tribe of Simeon during the time of the Exodus. He served as the head of his tribe at the census recorded in Numbers 1:6. His role as a tribal leader highlights his importance in organizing and representing the Simeonites during Israel's wilderness journey.
namesAndTitles: The name Shelumiel means 'G-d [El] is [my] peace,' revealing a theologically rich meaning that emphasizes God's peace as central to his identity. This proper name, recorded in Numbers 1:6, reflects a personal connection to God without indication that it was given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Shelumiel was the son of Zurishaddai, as noted in Numbers 1:6. Beyond this paternal relationship, no additional family details are provided in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Shelumiel's significance lies in his leadership during the Exodus, specifically as the appointed head of the tribe of Simeon at the time of the census. This position entrusted him with the responsibility of representing and organizing his tribe, contributing to the orderly arrangement of Israel's tribes under God's guidance. His mention in Numbers underscores the importance of tribal leadership in God's plan for His people during their wilderness journey.
